title: Recruiting at the Tavern
text: Both the monster merchant's trained hands and Siltvelt's envoys pitched in to help erect the larger tent, I say. A mixed-breed Lizardman listened to Father's instructions and began unloading baggage from the wagon. Father, of course, helped out alongside him. And naturally, I helped as well, indeed. The Filolial-samas, meanwhile, were all cheerfully chatting about the finer points of pulling carriages, having thoroughly enjoyed themselves. Then, like some lively musical troupe, they all practiced their singing together. It was quite the delightful sight.
“‘Piyo-piyo!’”

Yuki-chan and the others hopped about cheerfully as well. And so, the tent construction was nearing completion. Word that a circus had arrived drew a trickle of curious townsfolk to peek at our doings. The monster merchant's subordinates said they'd handle spreading the word around the area.
“Now then… the framework is coming along nicely, but Hero-sama… the slaves procured along the way are ready. Shall we proceed?”
Siltvelt's envoy proposed a quiet trip to Siltvelt.
“Understood. Father, I'll be off, indeed.”
“Yeah. I'll leave that sort of thing to you.”
“Then let's go! Portal Spear, I say!”
A swift shift in location!
We arrived in Siltvelt, indeed.
“Oh… this certainly is Siltvelt. Though the time seems different from Melromarc's.”
“Time difference, indeed.”
It's easy to forget, but the tilt of the sun does vary by location. So when you portal to a distant place, it can feel almost like you've leapt through time itself.
“I've observed this through communication reports, but experiencing an instantaneous move like this firsthand really does feel strange.”
Siltvelt's envoy murmured this and turned a glance toward the monster merchant's subordinate. It seemed they were about to make contact with the local monster merchants.
“Well then, we shall also see to our reports to the nation and various other matters. What will you do, Spear Hero-sama?”
Hmm… let's see.
“Piyo?”

Right now, we were in Siltvelt, indeed. And here, alongside the circus, slave trading was underway. Our main focus was the circus performances, and… if Kou kept growing up as he was, he might end up underestimating Father entirely, which could lead to some frightful consequences. Big Sister and the others were still recuperating and would eventually rejoin us, but that was still a point of concern. So, the personnel we needed… as far as putting on a show went, having Panda and Elephant around would be quite reassuring! Apparently they were mercenaries, so hiring them with money seemed the way to go. Though, given Melromarc's surveillance, some degree of caution was necessary.
“I have someone I'd like to recruit and bring along myself, so I'll go have a word, indeed.”
“And who might that be?”
“A capable instructor for the Filolial-samas, indeed.”

All to ensure Kou didn't grow up traumatized, I intended to recruit Elephant, who could provide the Filolial-samas with delightful singing sessions. Panda, meanwhile, would surely serve as Father's healing charm. Being skilled in performance, she could probably even do ball-balancing tricks. Big Sister and the others would likely help out once their health stabilized, but having Elephant around besides wouldn't hurt at all. And so, the recruitment of Elephant and Panda began. As far as timing went… relying on memory, they should have been in Siltvelt around this period. So, using Father's account from when he'd headed to Faubrey—having spotted Panda and Elephant there—as a reference, I searched centering around the inn they'd stayed at that time. Well now, Elephant's got quite the sizable build. Search around, and she'd turn up easily enough. Siltvelt was a melting pot of Demi-Humans and Beastmen, but focusing on the larger Beastmen narrowed things down fast. And so, relying on memory, I wandered about for several hours, and eventually found them.
“Heard the Shield Hero got framed for something and is lying low, but I wonder if it's gonna come to blows.”
Panda was drinking with her subordinates at a tavern, chatting away to Elephant.
“Not sure yet. Either way, I'm planning to move on soon myself.”
“Aw, what's with you? Being a killjoy.”
“That's my own business, isn't it. Well… once I wrap up some errands, I'll probably head toward Faubrey, and if I've got nothing better to do, back to Zeltoble.”
“Oh-ho… something going on?”
Elephant furrowed her brow at Panda, who was drinking in the rudest manner imaginable with her feet up on the table.
“Nothing's going on.”

Judging from Elephant's demeanor, something was clearly going on—probably sneaking off to secretly meet her former rat subordinates or something along those lines. She really is a good Elephant, I say. The rats' loyalty toward her ran deep, so there was no mistaking it.
“Yeah, yeah. If we meet in the arena, I'm not holding back, so brace yourself.”
“That's exactly what I should be saying to you. Don't get too lazy and drop dead somewhere out of nowhere—pace yourself a little.”
And so on, Elephant and Panda seemed to be chatting away together. That's when I approached and called out to them.
“Might I have a moment?”
“Huh?”
“…What?”
Panda and Elephant both turned suspicious eyes on me in unison.
“What's this? What business does this human have with our Big Sisters?”
“A guy who doesn't know his place.”
“Sounds like a death wish to me.”
Panda's subordinates whispered among themselves a short distance away.
“Hey. What business do you have with our Big Sister without telling us first?”
“I have business, so I called out to her, indeed. Do I need your permission for that?”
“Wha—”
“Talking to her without our permission—what nerve, you bastard!”

Hm, so Panda's subordinates require permission, do they? I glanced at Panda, but she wasn't affirming or denying anything, merely watching how things unfolded. Her reaction was quite different from when Father was around. Hmm… all things considered, Panda's subordinates were mostly there for odd jobs, so taking them down wouldn't be wise. More importantly, causing a clumsy ruckus could jeopardize the recruitment entirely. In that case… the best approach would be to threaten them with whatever they'd find most troubling. A negotiation technique passed down directly from Father, I say. I swiftly approached one of Panda's subordinates and whispered in his ear.
“Is that sort of attitude wise? I could reveal just what fun things happen when you get your beloved Big Sister thoroughly drunk, indeed.”
Twitch! The subordinate's ears shot up sharply, and he leapt back a considerable distance.
“Y-you bastard! How do you know about that!?”
“So, will I be granted permission?”
“O-oi…”
“I'll shut that mouth of yours! Come here!”
Oh? Seems that backfired.
“Hey, what'd he say to you?”
Another subordinate asked. The one who'd been spoken to whispered to his companions.
“Eh? Oi… this is bad, isn't it?”
“Trouble.”
“Should we silence him?”
“If you wish to fight, I'll oblige, indeed. I'll hold back so as not to kill you.”
“That's some nerve you've got!”
Bang! Panda's subordinate flipped the table over and cracked his knuckles.
“Piyo!”
“Piyo-piyo!”
I gently handed Yuki-chan and the others over to Elephant.
“Huh?”
Elephant, looking dumbfounded, cradled Yuki-chan and the others in her hands regardless. Truly, she's a good Elephant, indeed.
“Well then, let's finish this in one go! Hah!”
I swiftly circled behind Panda's subordinate, hooked my spear around his neck, and gave him a light smack.
“Ugwah!”
“What is this guy!? So freaking fast!”
“Surround him and beat him down!”
“Right!”
And with that, the remaining subordinates—minus the one who'd already been struck down—surrounded me and lunged.
“Cut it out!”
Whoosh! A bottle came flying between us.
“He's not someone you lot can handle. Besides, if we get banned from here right now, that'd be a real pain.”
Panda had stepped in to mediate the moment things got out of hand.
“But, Big Sister—”
“I said stand down.”
“Y-yes, ma'am.”
“O-oi. Don't you dare go spilling this to anyone, got it?”
Panda's subordinates, looking thoroughly reluctant, righted the table and went off to bow their heads to the tavern owner.
